question: Why does from_pymc(gil_free=True) sometimes not reproduce the draws of the compiled function it wraps (WP83: data_dims_det 0/3, ar1 2/3, simplex_bounded 2/3, one t1 != t4), and is there a single flag or cache step that makes it bit-identical?

models.source: models.py and callpath_targets.py copied verbatim from STUDIES/pymc_gil_free_default_v1 (WP83)

control.primary: callable_same_fn: the very PyTensor NUMBA function object that gil_free wraps (target.keep_alive[2]), called as a Python callable with from_pymc's own wrapper code, threads=1, in the same process. For data_dims_det this is the frozen (freeze_dims_and_data) graph, so the comparison is no longer between two different numba programs as in WP83.
control.secondary: wp83_control: owalnuts.from_pymc(model, mode='NUMBA') on a fresh build of the model (WP83's control: for data_dims_det the unfrozen graph), threads=1, same process; arm A only, descriptive.

cache_states: processes alternate cold (index even: before the process the parent deletes NUMBA_CACHE_DIR and PyTensor's base_compiledir, which holds PyTensor's numba cache) and warm (index odd: the cache left by the preceding cold process of the same arm and model).

D.label: cfunc compiled with PyTensor's fastmath flag set {arcp, contract, afn, reassoc, nsz} (package default: no fastmath on the wrapper)

E.label: PyTensor numba file cache off (every process compiles fresh)

T.label: thread arm: package as is, gil_free at threads 1 and 4 in every process

order.within: arm, then model in list order, then process index 0..n-1 (even cold, odd warm)

gradient_probe.definition: q0 (the model's unconstrained initial point) + 0.5 x N(0, I) from numpy default_rng(86); at each point the log density and gradient from the cfunc (through ctypes, as the sampler calls it) and from the wrapped PyTensor function; bit identity, max abs and ulp differences, and |diff| <= 1e-15 x max(1, |g|)

recorded: per process: cache file counts at start; PyTensor fastmath/cache config; the inner dispatcher's numba cache hits/misses; the cfunc's LLVM IR and assembly (size, sha256, fmuladd/fma and vfmadd counts, calls); the gradient probe; draw sha256 of gil_free t1, callable_same_fn t1 (and gil_free t4, wp83_control where the arm says); walls (descriptive, co-tenanted)

criteria.D2_wrapper_fidelity: in a process, gil_free t1 draws are bit-identical to callable_same_fn t1 draws and the gradient probe is bit-identical at all 50 points
criteria.D1_cross_process: for an (arm, model), every process gives the same gil_free t1 draw hash
criteria.D3_threads: in a process with gil_free t4, its draws are bit-identical to gil_free t1

predictions.H1: arm A: on the three affected models, D2 fails only in cold processes (every warm process passes D2); the unaffected models pass D2 in every process; where the gradient probe differs, the largest difference is <= 4 ulp
predictions.H2: arm A: callable_same_fn draws are identical across all 10 processes of a model (the compiled PyTensor function itself is deterministic); the cross-process variation (D1 failures) is in the cfunc only
predictions.H3: arm B (fastmath off) passes D1 and D2 on all 5 models x 10 processes
predictions.H4: arms C (error_model) and D (wrapper fastmath) do not remove the cold-process mismatches
predictions.H5: arm E (no file cache) passes D1 but fails D2 on the affected models in every process (every process behaves as cold)
predictions.H6: arm T: D3 holds in all 60 processes (WP83's t1 != t4 was a cold process against a warm one), while D2 fails only in cold processes as in H1
predictions.mechanism: on a cold compile the cfunc links the freshly compiled PyTensor function's LLVM IR, inlines it and re-optimises it under PyTensor's per-instruction fastmath flags (contraction / reassociation), so the cfunc's arithmetic differs from the separately compiled dispatcher's; on a warm process the dispatcher comes from the cache and the cfunc calls the same object code. The LLVM/asm evidence (IR size, fmuladd and vfmadd counts, calls) is recorded to test this.

fix_rule.candidates: arms B, C, D, E (each a single flag) and the cache-warming step (arm A restricted to warm processes, descriptive: it cannot be shipped as a package change because the package cannot guarantee a warm cache)
fix_rule.qualifies_iff: D2 holds in every one of the 50 processes (5 models x 10) and D1 holds for every model
fix_rule.if_one_or_more_qualify: propose the qualifying flag as a package change in owalnuts.from_pymc(gil_free=True), behind nothing (a correctness fix); preference order C, D (wrapper-local, no effect on the user's PyTensor configuration), then B (applied by compiling gil_free's function under pytensor.config.change_flags(numba__fastmath=False)), then E (change_flags(numba__cache=False)); the wall-per-gradient cost of the proposed flag against arm A (median over processes) is reported
fix_rule.if_none_qualify: document the caveat precisely in the from_pymc docstring and the docs: which models, which cache state, what size of difference, and what does reproduce

rules: PREREGISTRATION.md and protocol.json committed before the first evidence process. Lane setup (venv with the WP78 pins, the extension built from the frozen commit) and a smoke run on the non-study model 'poisson' are infrastructure and disclosed. Every process is reported; failures and timeouts are results; no reruns, no tuning after seeing results. A process with no record may be rerun once, recorded as a deviation. Amendments only for processes not yet run, committed before them.
